decision_basis: The two identified non-target stratigraphic levels in B100NC-1 enclose at most 151.25 − 137.5 = 13.75 cm. Uses the primary Table 2 bracket without assuming which bed contact 147.5 cm represents.
qualification: Requires correct stratigraphy, capture of primary fallout within the bracket and negligible loss/compaction for transfer to original thickness. Use a lake station as location proxy, not the volcano summit; double bound and omit in sensitivities.

decision_basis: Johnson et al. identify about 20 cm as primary fallout at the pure flat-topped lower Meadow mine cut. No averaging of the 38 holes.
qualification: Author estimate. Assumes the clean cut preserves the local total. Disturbed channel fills, slopewash and missing beds in other holes are excluded. Use the actual legal-section footprint for location checks.

decision_basis: The May 1985 core places the entire identified ash interval between 282 and 345 cm. Later input is documented. Under full primary capture, the 63 cm preserved total is a ceiling on its primary share.
qualification: Assumes primary fallout was sufficiently retained in this interval at the deep meromictic basin and bulk compaction/loss is negligible. Prolonged enrichment and other descriptions of 70–80 cm make the conversion conditional. Compare weaker upper and omission.

decision_basis: The field guide describes a mature outwash soil and lag buried by approximately 50 cm of Mazama ash. A climactic portion of the retained package cannot exceed its total under the stated preservation assumptions.
qualification: An approximate field ceiling. Requires retention of the climactic deposit and negligible net thinning/compaction; earlier or imported material could inflate the total. Double the ceiling and omit in sensitivities; exact face offset from the turnoff unreported.
